bull.b: Affirm’s scaled operating and free cash flow provides capacity to fund product development, support loan origination and reduce reliance on external financing. Persistence would strengthen resilience across funding and credit cycles.

Lower leverage and a larger equity base improve financial flexibility for a lending platform exposed to funding markets. The stronger capitalization can support growth investments and provide greater capacity to absorb credit or liquidity shocks.

Growth across Pay-in-X and Affirm Card indicates expanding product usage and deeper customer engagement. Higher card spend and broader installment adoption can improve monetization and strengthen Affirm’s role within merchant checkout.

bear.b: A severe annual revenue contraction raises questions about the durability of growth, revenue mix and reporting comparability. Even with improving cash flow, inconsistent top-line performance could constrain planning and weaken confidence in future expansion.

Conflicting margin disclosures make it harder to assess the quality and recurrence of reported profitability. Reduced visibility into underlying unit economics may limit confidence that recent earnings improvements will persist across future periods.

Physical-retail integration friction and still-limited merchant penetration can delay broader network expansion. Additional engineering, enterprise sales and integration work may be required before offline adoption becomes a meaningful, scalable growth driver.
